jobs.description_html:
Description

Keeper Security is hiring a Senior Compliance Program Manager to join our CISO organization and help drive regulatory compliance, audit readiness and security governance across Keeper’s enterprise and federal environments. This is a 100% remote position from select locations, with an opportunity to work a hybrid schedule for candidates based in the Chicago, IL or El Dorado Hills, CA metro areas.

Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and help strengthen the compliance and governance programs that support Keeper’s enterprise and public sector customers.

 

About Keeper

 

Keeper Security is a leading cybersecurity software company that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in more than 150 countries. Keeper delivers a powerful zero-trust and zero-knowledge solution built to meet the stringent requirements of federal IT environments. Its flagship offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects users, devices, and critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized in the Gartner® Magic QuadrantTM for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper combines robust compliance with unmatched visibility and control. With industry-leading certifications, including FedRAMP High and GovRAMP Moderate Authorization, Keeper provides the security assurance public sector organizations require. Learn why federal agencies, including NASA and the DOJ, trust Keeper to defend against today’s sophisticated adversaries at KeeperSecurity.com.    



About the Role

As a Senior Compliance Program Manager, you will manage complex compliance and governance initiatives across Keeper’s enterprise and regulated environments, including FedRAMP High and DoD IL5.

You will be responsible for coordinating audit cycles, continuous monitoring, POA&M remediation, third-party risk, policy governance, security training and supporting documentation. You will work closely with control owners and security leadership to translate regulatory requirements into clear plans, operational processes and accountable workstreams. This role requires strong compliance expertise combined with disciplined program management. You will maintain integrated plans, track risks and dependencies, drive cross-functional accountability and ensure documentation, training and evidence remain accurate, complete and audit-ready.

Responsibilities

  • Plan and manage compliance programs across audit cycles, continuous monitoring, POA&M remediation, policy initiatives and supporting documentation
  • Establish program scope, milestones, dependencies, ownership and reporting across Security, Engineering, DevOps, IT and GRC
  • Maintain integrated program plans, risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies and escalate blockers with clear recommendations
  • Coordinate evidence collection, remediation tracking and control-owner activities for compliance and audit initiatives
  • Maintain working knowledge of frameworks including NIST 800-53, FedRAMP High, DoD IL5, SOC 2, ISO 27001 and PCI DSS
  • Partner with GRC and ISSO stakeholders on audit readiness, control documentation, remediation and continuous monitoring activities
  • Monitor evolving regulatory and security requirements and assess potential business and operational impact
  • Support compliance responses for customers, contracts, security reviews and RFPs
  • Support and help mature Keeper’s third-party risk management program, including risk-tiered assessments of vendors and business partners
  • Review vendor security documentation, attestations and supply chain risk factors and provide risk-based recommendations
  • Partner with Procurement, Legal and business owners on security requirements, contract terms and remediation expectations
  • Maintain the third-party risk register and track remediation, risk acceptance and program metrics
  • Author, maintain and govern information security policies, standards, procedures and control narratives
  • Support System Security Plan documentation and other compliance-related technical documentation
  • Develop and maintain information security training for employees and role-specific audiences including developers, administrators, privileged users and incident responders
  • Manage training lifecycle activities including scheduling, learning management system administration, completion tracking, phishing simulation and audit evidence
  • Develop training materials, job aids, scenarios and assessments in partnership with subject matter experts
  • Measure and report training effectiveness using completion, assessment and behavioral metrics
  • Collaborate with Engineering and Product teams to validate technical information and maintain accurate, audit-ready documentation
  • Translate complex technical and regulatory information into clear documentation for auditors, leadership and internal stakeholders
  • Mentor team members and cross-functional partners on compliance processes and documentation practices
  • Use AI-assisted tools such as Claude, ChatGPT or similar platforms to improve regulatory research, documentation, analysis, training development and workflow efficiency

Requirements

  • 6+ years of progressive experience in information security compliance, governance, risk, audit, program management or a related field
  • 3+ years of experience leading audits, assessments or compliance initiatives involving NIST 800-53, FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001 or similar frameworks
  • Strong working knowledge of NIST 800-53 Rev. 5, NIST RMF, FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001 and related compliance requirements
  • Experience managing complex cross-functional compliance programs from planning through completion
  • Experience supporting regulated or federal cloud environments, ideally including FedRAMP High, DoD IL4/IL5 or similar requirements
  • Experience with authorization documentation such as System Security Plans, POA&Ms, continuous monitoring artifacts or related evidence
  • Experience supporting or managing third-party risk management programs
  • Experience developing and governing information security policies, standards and procedures
  • Experience developing or delivering information security training for technical and non-technical audiences
  • Strong program management skills including planning, scheduling, risk and issue management, dependency tracking and stakeholder communication
  • Strong documentation governance skills, including managing reviews, approvals, versioning and controlled release
  • Strong ability to interpret technical and regulatory requirements and translate them into actionable operational guidance
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with experience communicating with executives, auditors and technical stakeholders
  • Ability to work independently, manage multiple concurrent initiatives and influence cross-functional stakeholders without direct authority
  • Ability and willingness to use AI-assisted tools effectively to support compliance research, documentation, analysis and program execution
  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Information Systems, Computer Science, Business Administration, Technical Communication or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • At least one relevant professional certification such as PMP, CISSP, CISA, CISM, CRISC, CGRC or ISO 27001 Lead Auditor

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience supporting FedRAMP High or DoD IL5 authorization and continuous monitoring activities
  • Experience with NIST 800-53 AT controls and security awareness or role-based training programs
  • Experience with supply chain risk management and vendor security assessments
  • Familiarity with security contract requirements, data protection addenda and federal flow-down requirements
  • Experience with phishing simulation platforms, learning management systems or compliance automation platforms
  • Experience preparing customer-facing compliance or security responses
  • Familiarity with NIST SP 800-50, NIST SP 800-16 or related security training guidance
  • Additional security, audit, risk or project management certifications

Benefits

  • Employer Paid Life Insurance & Employee/Spouse/Child Supplemental life

  • A generous PTO plan that celebrates your commitment and seniority (including paid Bereavement/Jury Duty, etc)

Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and is sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and bring your IL5 DevOps expertise to mission-critical work.

About Keeper

Keeper Security is transforming cybersecurity for organizations globally with zero-trust privileged access management built with end-to-end encryption. Keeper’s cybersecurity solutions are FedRAMP and StateRAMP Authorized, SOC 2 compliant, FIPS 140-2 validated, as well as ISO 27001, 27017 and 27018 certified. Keeper deploys in minutes, not months, and seamlessly integrates with any tech stack to prevent breaches, reduce help desk costs and ensure compliance. You will collaborate closely with security engineering, platform engineering, and compliance teams to deliver highly available, resilient, and audit-ready systems in AWS GovCloud and/or Azure Government environments. You will work as an embedded member of the DevOps organization and apply software engineering principles to infrastructure validation, release confidence and operational resilience. You will develop reusable validation frameworks, automate testing of infrastructure-as-code, verify cloud and networking changes, test failure and recovery scenarios and integrate automated safeguards into CI/CD workflows.   • Test Kubernetes and containerized environments for configuration, reliability, scalability and security

  • Experience integrating automation into CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI or similar technologies

  • Experience troubleshooting infrastructure and distributed-system issues using logs, metrics and observability platforms such as Datadog
  • Experience with Git-based software development workflows, pull requests, peer review and automated delivery practices
  • Understanding of reliability concepts including fault tolerance, failure recovery, deployment safety and operational resilience
  • Familiarity with security hardening or compliance requirements such as CIS benchmarks, DISA STIGs, FedRAMP, SOC 2 or ISO 27001

Kivo Health is building a tech-enabled healthcare clinic to help real people breathe better, using innovative technology to make a lasting impact. We're YC-backed and well-funded, and looking for a fullstack engineer to join our small, high-leverage engineering team in Seattle.

You'll work alongside a diverse team of industry experts in healthcare and startup technology. Our engineering team is intentionally small and made up of generalists rather than specialists, so you'll move fluidly across dev tooling, product features, and core web app work. Our stack includes Python/Django on the backend and TypeScript, React, and React Native across web and mobile. This is an in-office, Seattle-based role.

jobs.description_html:
We Breathe Life Into Data

At Komodo Health, our mission is to reduce the global burden of disease. And we believe that smarter use of data is essential to this mission. That’s why we built the Healthcare Map — the industry’s largest, most complete, precise view of the U.S. healthcare system — by combining de-identified, real-world patient data with innovative algorithms and decades of clinical experience. The Healthcare Map serves as our foundation for a powerful suite of software applications, helping us answer healthcare’s most complex questions for our partners. Across the healthcare ecosystem, we’re helping our clients unlock critical insights to track detailed patient behaviors and treatment patterns, identify gaps in care, address unmet patient needs, and reduce the global burden of disease. 

As we pursue these goals, it remains essential to us that we stay grounded in our values: be awesome, seek growth, deliver “wow,” and enjoy the ride. At Komodo, you will be joining a team of ambitious, supportive Dragons with diverse backgrounds but a shared passion to deliver on our mission to reduce the burden of disease — and enjoy the journey along the way.

The Opportunity at Komodo Health

Komodo Health's AI Platform and Services organization builds the platform every AI product at Komodo runs on: agent infrastructure, evals, data context, and the surfaces customers touch. Small pods build on shared primitives and ship in weeks. Product managers here build the first versions of what they propose and to iterate alongside their teams quickly.

The suite that built this business was designed for an analyst at a screen. The platform underneath it now reasons. Our flagship product Navigator runs investigations that used to take a person weeks, and an ai-augmented product suite interoperates with it to streamline workflows. We are just getting started. What the next generation of the suite actually is remains an open question, and today it needs ownership.

That question is this seat. You will define the next generation of Komodo's product suite and prove it by building it. The current surfaces are your material and your distribution. The mandate is what comes after them. Principal here means your answer sets the pattern for every surface that follows. This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You will lead through your thesis and your builds, embedded in small engineering pods, not through a team of direct reports.

Looking back on your first 12 months at Komodo Health, you will have…

  • Put a thesis on record for what the next generation of the suite is, argued in working software customers have touched, and won cross-functional and leadership support for it.
  • Built the first version of at least two new products from that thesis yourself, then ran a pod of four or fewer from prototype to GA with no dedicated project management.
  • Those products live in customer environments, with measurable revenue, adoption, or retention impact.
  • Made the current suite smaller. At least one existing legacy solution retired or folded into its successor, without customer churn.
  • You will accomplish these outcomes through the following responsibilities:
  • Own the thesis for what customers touch. Study how they actually work, decide what should exist, and revise the argument as models improve.
  • Build first versions with AI tools and platform primitives. Bring engineering in to scale what shows value, and drop what does not.
  • Work inside customer environments when the problem calls for it, scope in real time while contracts are being negotiated, and treat deployment as part of the product.
  • Propose and defend the shape of the growing portfolio. As the new generation lands, you decide what the existing solutions become.
  • Package for the field. Partner with sales and marketing on what we sell, run the market analysis behind it, and make sure every new product can be positioned, enabled, and sold.
  • Set the pattern. Your architecture and your build habits become how the surface pods around you work.

What you bring to Komodo Health (required):

  • Builds the first version. You will show us something you built, not something you managed, this is evaluated in the interview.
  • AI native at product depth. You can reason at a low level about the AI products you intend to ship: context and grounding, evals and quality gates, agent behavior, and cost. Using chat tools to work faster is the baseline everywhere, so it earns nothing here.
  • Comfortable inside customer environments and contracting cycles, with the judgment to commit responsibly in real time.
  • Zero to one at Principal  scope. 10+ years in product, including at least one product you conceived and shipped that earns real revenue today. We will ask what existed before it, and what was retired to make room for it.
  • Excellent written communication. Your reasoning gets adopted because it is clear.

Additional skills and experience we’d prioritize (nice to have)…

  • Healthcare or regulated data experience (claims, EHR, patient journeys, provider analytics), or a track record of getting fluent fast in a comparably complex data domain like supply chain, energy, or financial data. Time at a company through a platform transition. Experience retiring a product without losing its customers.
  • Experience interacting with, managing, or building with AI agentic workflows

Across the healthcare ecosystem, we’re helping our clients unlock critical insights to track detailed patient behaviors and treatment patterns, identify gaps in care, address unmet patient needs, and reduce the global burden of disease. 

As we pursue these goals, it remains essential to us that we stay grounded in our values: be awesome, seek growth, deliver “wow,” and enjoy the ride. At Komodo, you will be joining a team of ambitious, supportive Dragons with diverse backgrounds but a shared passion to deliver on our mission to reduce the burden of disease — and enjoy the journey along the way.

The Opportunity at Komodo Health:

The Platform team owns Komodo’s core control plane – KMC/PSS, identity and access, subscription lifecycle, and the SDKs and tools that power all the Komodo products such as App Builder and Connector, Maplab, Sentinel, Marmot . We provide the foundations that internal teams and customers use to onboard, manage access, and build on top of Komodo’s data. Our work enables 150+ client organizations and internal product teams to operate reliably, securely, and efficiently at scale.

This Staff Engineer role exists to lead the technical direction across KMC/PSS and App Builder + Connector, ensuring our platform is reliable, secure, cost-efficient, and easy to build on. They will partner closely with Product, FDE, and customer-facing teams to turn complex onboarding and platform requirements into robust, well-documented systems. This role is a key part of how we scale self-service onboarding, expand our platform surface area, and ultimately reduce the burden of disease by making Komodo’s data and services more accessible.

Looking back on your first 12 months at Komodo Health, you will have accomplished…

  • Developed a deep understanding of the platform, our internal/external customers, and how KMC, Connector, and App Builder fit into Komodo’s product ecosystem.
  • Owned and delivered at least one major subscription service initiative (for example, My Subscriptions enhancements, self-service SAML SSO, or new admin workflows), improving time-to-onboard and operator efficiency for internal teams.
  • Become the go-to technical owner of core platform contracts (APIs, data models, events, and RBAC patterns) for subscription services and related platform workflows, reducing integration friction and ambiguity for downstream product teams.
  • Architected and deployed custom MCP (Model Context Protocol) tooling and autonomous agents, enabling seamless data interoperability between internal systems and AI models to automate complex platform engineering tasks.
  • Contributed to the development of secure, reliable API endpoints and platform services, solving key development and deployment challenges to make platform infrastructure highly reliable, easy to maintain, and cost-effective.
  • Defined and improved monitoring, alerting, and observability for platform services and actively participated in the on-call rotation to support production systems.
  • Acted as the escalation point for complex, cross-system incidents touching KMC, Connector, and App Builder, combining fast triage with deeper investigation to protect customer experience and platform reliability.
  • Collaborated effectively with cross-functional teams (solution architects, forward-deployed engineers, customer success, and product) to support new feature rollouts and integrate authentication services with various APIs and external systems.
  • Implemented measures to enhance developer experience, such as well-documented code, clear API documentation, efficient debugging tools, and the adoption of AI-powered development and operations workflows (e.g., Cursor, Claude, and Gemini) that measurably improved developer productivity and reduced MTTR for the Platform team.

What you bring to Komodo Health (required):

  • Engineering Excellence: Expert-level backend engineering experience (Python + FastAPI preferred) building and operating APIs and microservices at scale, with strong debugging and technical troubleshooting skills.
  • Platform & Control Plane Experience: Proven track record designing and evolving core platform primitives (e.g., authentication/authorization, orgs/accounts, subscriptions, or similar control-plane systems) in a multi-tenant SaaS environment.
  • Cloud Infrastructure: Profound experience with AWS core services and the ability to architect secure, scalable, and cost-efficient solutions from high-level requirements.
  • Data & Observability: Familiarity with modern data platforms and workflow tools (e.g., Snowflake, Airflow, Spark) and an understanding of how to design for observability (metrics, logs, traces, events) across complex distributed systems.
  • System Design & Tradeoffs: Ability to design solutions that thoughtfully balance non-functional concerns such as performance, cost, maintainability, reliability, and developer experience.
  • Leadership & Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to drive complex, cross-team projects to completion, mentor other engineers, and collaborate effectively with product managers, data scientists, and customer-facing teams.
  • AI & Productivity: Comfort leveraging AI tools (e.g., Cursor, ChatGPT, Gemini) and interest in integrating LLM-based workflows into the SDLC to improve engineering velocity and quality.

Additional skills and experience we’d prioritize (nice to have)

  • Experience with AWS preferred. AWS cloud infrastructure certification is a plus. 
  • Experience with data privacy concerns such as HIPAA or GDPR
  • Working knowledge of data modeling and storage across relational (PostgreSQL), NoSQL (DynamoDB, Redis), and MPP databases (Snowflake, Redshift).
  • Prior experience in platform or infrastructure teams supporting internal and external developers, including SDKs, CLIs, and self-service tooling.
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams and with other customer-facing teams
  • Passion! We hope you are passionate about our mission and technology
  • Ownership! We hope you own your work, be accountable, and push it through the finish line. We hope you treat yourself as a cofounder and do not hesitate to share any idea that helps Komodo
  • Expertise! We do not need you to know everything, but we hope you have deep knowledge in at least one area and can start contributing quickly. And we would love to learn from you in your area(s) of expertise as well.

The pay range for each job posting reflects a minimum and maximum range of annual base pay that we reasonably expect to pay for this position within the US. We carefully consider multiple business-related factors when determining compensation, including job-related skills, work experience, geographic work location, relevant training and certifications, business needs and market demands.

 

The starting annual base pay for this role is listed below. This position may be eligible for performance-based bonuses as determined in the Company’s sole discretion and in accordance with a written agreement or plan. This role may also be eligible for equity awards. In addition, this role is eligible for benefits including, but not limited to, comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance; flexible time off and holidays; 401(k) with company match; disability insurance and life insurance; and leaves of absence in accordance with applicable state and local laws and regulations and company policy. 

San Francisco Bay Area and New York City:

Komodo's AI Standard

At Komodo, we're not just witnessing the AI revolution – we're leading it. This is a pivotal moment in time, where being first to market with AI transforms industries and sets the bar. We've already established industry leadership in leveraging AI to revolutionize healthcare, and we expect every team member to contribute. AI here isn't optional; it's foundational. We expect you to integrate AI into your daily work – from summarizing documents to automating workflows and uncovering insights. This isn't just about efficiency; it's about making every moment more meaningful, building on trust in AI, and driving our collective success.

Join us in shaping the future of healthcare intelligence.

jobs.description_html:
About Mach Industries

Founded in 2023, Mach Industries is a rapidly growing defense technology company focused on developing next-generation autonomous defense platforms. At the core of our mission is the commitment to delivering scalable, decentralized defense systems that enhance the strategic capabilities of the United States and its allies. With a workforce of approximately 350 employees, we operate with startup agility and ambition.

Our vision is to redefine the future of warfare through cutting-edge manufacturing, innovation at speed, and unwavering focus on national security. We are dedicated to solving the next generation of warfare with lethal systems that deter kinetic conflict and protect global security.

The Role

We’re hiring our first DevOps Engineer to build and own the infrastructure layer that powers everything we do — from developer velocity to production uptime. You’ll design, implement, and maintain the systems and tooling that keep our software lifecycle secure, scalable, and fast. This is a foundational hire: you’ll be given wide technical latitude and trusted to help shape our DevOps culture, tooling, and long-term approach to reliability and automation.

We're looking for someone who loves enabling engineering teams through thoughtful infrastructure design, has strong opinions about CI/CD and observability best practices, and thrives in a high-trust, fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain Github CI/CD pipelines to accelerate developer velocity and minimize deployment risk.

  • Architect and manage cloud infrastructure (AWS) for high availability, scalability, and security.

  • Monitor and improve system observability: logging, metrics, alerting, on-call response.

  • Collaborate with software and hardware teams to support test infrastructure, simulation environments, and production deployments.

  • Lead the implementation of best practices in infrastructure security and cost optimization.

  • Establish incident response protocols and support root cause analysis.

  • Help shape DevOps processes, tools, and team culture as we scale.

Required Qualifications 

  • 3+ years of experience in a DevOps, Infrastructure, or SRE role.

  • Proficiency with cloud platforms like AWS.

  • Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using tools like GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, etc.

  • Strong background in scripting (e.g. Python, Bash).

  • Solid understanding of containerization (Docker) and orchestration (e.g. Kubernetes or ECS).

  • Familiarity with system observability tools (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, Datadog, etc.).

  • Excellent debugging and incident management skills.

  • Comfortable owning large initiatives end-to-end with minimal oversight.

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience supporting production systems in a defense, robotics, or hardware-adjacent environment.

  • Knowledge of airgapped or secure deployment environments.

  • Familiarity with compliance standards (e.g. FedRAMP, NIST 800-171, or CMMC).

  • Exposure to embedded systems build pipelines or cross-compilation toolchains.

  • Passion for automation, infrastructure design, and enabling engineering teams.

  • Experience in infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Terraform, CloudFormation).

Additional Requirements

  • Available to work extended hours and weekends as needed

With a workforce of approximately 350 employees, we operate with startup agility and ambition.

Our vision is to redefine the future of warfare through cutting-edge manufacturing, innovation at speed, and unwavering focus on national security. We are dedicated to solving the next generation of warfare with lethal systems that deter kinetic conflict and protect global security.

The Role

We are seeking an Engineering Program Manager (EPM) to own the programmatic mechanics of a vehicle program — schedule tracking, risk and issue management, review cadence, and cross-functional coordination — so that the Chief Engineer's time stays focused on technical authority rather than schedule bookkeeping. You will act as the Chief Engineer's execution counterpart: surfacing schedule and resourcing risk before it becomes a problem, keeping Department Heads and the Capability Development Manager (CDM) in sync with program status, and ensuring that commitments made to leadership and the customer are grounded in what the schedule and risk register actually show.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the day-to-day program mechanics of a vehicle: schedule tracking, the risk/issue register, review cadence, and cross-functional coordination logistics.
  • Own how the program tracks and reports schedule, risk, and dependencies, along with key metrics and KPIs.
  • Own the timeline for SRR, CODR, PDR, and CDR — content ownership of each review stays with the Chief Engineer and Responsible Engineers; the EPM owns how the program tracks and reports against that timeline.
  • Track overall program cost and budget alongside Finance.
  • Surface schedule and resourcing risk to the Chief Engineer and relevant Department Heads as soon as it becomes visible in the tracking data, rather than at the next scheduled review.
  • Coordinate cross-functionally between Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Finance, and Staffing on behalf of a given vehicle program.
  • Provide consolidated, accurate program status updates to company leadership, Growth team, and customers.
  • Coordinate closely with the Capability Development Manager (CDM) to keep customer-facing commitments and internal schedule tracking in sync.
  • Route scope changes or additional resourcing requests to the relevant Department Head for review before they're reflected in the schedule.
  • Jointly escalate, alongside the Chief Engineer and Department Head, any schedule or resourcing risk that can't be resolved between them — providing the supporting data for that escalation.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience in a program or project management role on a hardware, engineering, or technical product — ideally one with multiple concurrent workstreams and cross-functional dependencies.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain schedule, risk, and dependency tracking that technical leadership actually trusts and uses.
  • Comfort surfacing bad news early — flagging schedule slip or risk as soon as it's visible rather than smoothing it over until a review forces the conversation.
  • Strong cross-functional coordination skills, with experience working across engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and finance stakeholders.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to translate program-tracking detail into a concise status narrative for leadership.

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Background in aerospace, defense, or another regulated hardware industry with formal design-review gates (SRR, CODR, PDR, CDR or equivalents).
  • Experience partnering directly with a technical architecture owner (Chief Engineer or equivalent) as their execution counterpart, rather than owning the technical decisions themselves.
  • Experience coordinating with a customer-facing or account-management counterpart (e.g., a CDM, TAM, or customer program manager) to keep external and internal timelines aligned.
  • Familiarity with formal risk/issue register tooling and structured schedule-tracking methods (critical path, earned value, etc.).
  • Prior experience navigating a scope or resourcing conflict jointly with technical and departmental leadership, rather than unilaterally.

Additional Requirements

  • Available to work extended hours and weekends as needed

Our vision is to redefine the future of warfare through cutting-edge manufacturing, innovation at speed, and unwavering focus on national security. We are dedicated to solving the next generation of warfare with lethal systems that deter kinetic conflict and protect global security.

The Role

Mach Industries is building an AI-forward autonomy stack for contested environments where GPS and other sensing are unavailable or unreliable. As a Machine Learning Engineer, you will own and scale the training, data, and edge-inference backbone that every vision and multi-sensor model on our product lines depends on for detection, tracking, search, navigation, targeting, and automatic target recognition. This is a broad, high-ownership role: you'll stand up the data and training infrastructure that lets the autonomy team iterate fast, generate synthetic data to cover the long tail, and get research-grade models running in real time on embedded hardware in flight. We are generalists, so you'll move fluidly between infrastructure, modeling, and deployment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own and evolve the training and data infrastructure the autonomy team builds on: ingestion from flight/sim/HITL, curation and mining, labeling/QA workflows, dataset versioning (DVC/Parquet), and reproducible dataset builds.

  • Stand up and scale training/eval infrastructure: distributed multi-GPU training, experiment tracking, a model registry, and CI-based evaluation with regression gates plus automated field-data to retrain to validate to redeploy loops.

  • Deploy and optimize models for real-time edge inference on Jetson-class hardware (quantization/pruning, TensorRT/ONNX Runtime); profile CPU/GPU and hit tight latency, throughput, and SWaP targets.

  • Build and improve models across the portfolio as a hands-on IC: detection, segmentation, tracking, target/area search, classification/ATR, and multi-sensor fusion for EO/IR and auxiliary sensing.

  • Generate and manage synthetic data at scale (simulation + domain randomization) to cover long-tail and degraded conditions and close sim-to-real gaps.

  • Instrument runtime health, drift detection, and graceful degradation, and wire model-performance metrics back into the data and retraining loop.

  • Live close to flight data with visualization, triage, and root-cause tooling so the team can go from field logs to insight and model updates rapidly.

  • Partner with other autonomy disciplines across perception, localization, embedded, and flight-test to take capabilities from prototype to sim to HITL to flight to deployment.

Required Qualifications

  • Strong generalist software engineering: Python for ML and tooling, plus production C++ on Linux; profiling, optimization, and rigorous testing discipline.

  • Proven experience building ML data and training pipelines end to end: dataset construction, labeling/QA, augmentation, experiment tracking, and reproducible training.

  • Hands-on training and fine-tuning in PyTorch across modern detection/segmentation/tracking architectures (CNN/Transformer).

  • Edge and real-time deployment: model compression (INT8/FP16), runtime optimization (TensorRT/ONNX Runtime), and meeting latency/SWaP constraints on embedded GPU (Jetson-class) hardware.

  • Data and MLOps infrastructure: SQL/Parquet, dataset/versioning tools, CI-based validation, and scalable multi-GPU training.

  • BS/MS/PhD in CS/EE/Robotics or similar, or equivalent experience, with a track record shipping ML models to production or hardware. Senior candidates: deeper ownership of training/data infrastructure at scale.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Synthetic data generation and simulation (e.g. Unreal/Isaac, domain randomization) and demonstrated sim-to-real transfer.

  • EO/IR imagery experience and working with real flight/test data in challenging, degraded, or contested environments.

  • Multi-modal perception and fusion (EO/IR + radar/LiDAR/RF) at the feature or decision level.

  • Detection/tracking/search at scale; active learning and data-mining strategies for long-tail coverage.

  • CUDA backends for performance debugging; ROS 2; NVIDIA Jetson deployment pipelines.

  • Drift/dataset-shift monitoring, robustness and rare-event testing, long-horizon reliability metrics.

  • Distributed training frameworks and cloud ML platforms (e.g. SageMaker); Docker for reproducibility; Rust for systems tooling.

As a Site Reliability Engineer at Material Security, you'll own the reliability of the infrastructure every product team builds on, including GCP, Kubernetes, and Postgres across hundreds of GCP projects. This is a software engineering role, where you’ll be building systems and the culture that removes manual on-call work, fixes the underlying causes of alerts, and gives engineers a clear view of system health. You'll work with every team and work with leadership to decide where things go..

Responsibilities

  • Design and build software that removes manual on-call intervention and recurring sources of toil.

  • Lead infrastructure projects end to end.

  • Find where cost-driven limits create latency or reliability problems, and fix the trade-off.

  • Build tooling that shows system health across our GCP projects at a glance.

  • Define SLOs with product teams and raise the bar on reliability practice across engineering.

  • Pioneer reliability engineering for agent-first production systems.

What We’re Looking For

  • Technical Ability: Solid software engineering fundamentals and raw coding ability. Production code is your default way of solving a problem.

  • Infrastructure Depth: Hands-on experience running GCP (or a comparable cloud) and Kubernetes at production scale, including autoscaling and capacity management.

  • Automation First: You have built tools and automation that other engineers depended on, not just runbooks that describe a manual fix.

  • Ownership: Comfortable driving ambiguous, cross-team reliability work on your own, from diagnosis to a shipped fix.

jobs.title: Design Lead, Consumer
jobs.description_html:
Maven Clinic is the world's largest virtual clinic for women and families on a mission to make healthcare work for all of us. Through Maven Enterprise, the company partners with more than 2,300 employers and health plans to provide end-to-end women's and family health programs spanning fertility and family building, maternity and newborn care, parenting and pediatrics, and menopause and midlife — improving clinical outcomes, reducing healthcare costs, and expanding equitable access to high-quality care at scale. Through its consumer platform, Maven provides direct access to virtual care across 30+ specialties, as well as dedicated hormone and GLP-1 care programs purpose-built for women. Founded in 2014 by CEO Kate Ryder, Maven Clinic has raised more than $425 million from leading healthcare and technology investors including General Catalyst, Sequoia, Dragoneer Investment Group, Oak HC/FT, StepStone Group, Icon Ventures, and Lux Capital. Recognized for innovation and industry leadership, Maven has been named to the TIME100 Most Influential Companies, CNBC Disruptor 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, and FORTUNE Best Places to Work. Learn more at mavenclinic.com

An award-winning culture working towards an important mission –  Maven Clinic is a recipient of over 30 workplace and innovation awards, including: 

  • TIME 100 Most Influential Companies (2023, 2026)
  • Fortune Change the World (2024)
  • CNBC Disruptor 50 List (2022, 2023, 2024)
  • Fortune Best Workplaces for Millennials (2024)
  • Fortune Best Workplaces in Health Care (2024)
  • Fast Company Most Innovative Companies (2020, 2023)
  • Fortune Best Workplaces NY (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)

About the role

We have recently launched our direct-to-consumer platform that gives women access to GLP-1 care, hormone care, and 30+ healthcare specialties, connecting metabolic, hormonal, reproductive, mental, and physical health in one care experience. We are building for women who are tired of fragmented care, unclear pricing, limited follow-up, and healthcare experiences that treat each symptom or life stage in isolation.

What You'll Do:

  • We’re looking for a founding Product Design Lead to help build and scale Maven’s direct-to-consumer healthcare experiences.
  • This role sits at the intersection of consumer growth, healthcare access, product craft, AI-native ways of working, and trust-sensitive design.
  • It is a hands-on player-coach role with formal line management responsibility. You’ll lead a small team of senior Product Design/UXR practitioners while also owning high-priority product design work yourself.
  • You’ll report to the General Manager, Consumer and partner closely with Product, Engineering, Growth, Data, Clinical, Legal, Operations, and Support teams.
  • You will help Maven compete in a fast-moving and highly competitive consumer healthcare market while staying true to what makes Maven different: connected, clinically responsible, whole-person care for women.
  • You will be designing for users who are actively comparing options, making decisions quickly, weighing affordability, navigating uncertainty, and deciding whether they trust Maven enough to start and continue care.
  • The work will span both 0→1 product development and continuous optimization of live consumer journeys. You’ll help define new journeys, shape concepts, prototype, and bring new consumer healthcare offerings to market, while also improving existing funnels, onboarding, eligibility, pricing, payment, prescription, activation, retention, and cross-sell experiences through research, experimentation, data, and design craft.

What You'll Bring:

  • 7+ years of product design experience, including complex consumer product journeys and 0→1 product growth.
  • Experience formally managing or leading design teams.
  • Strong hands-on product design craft across UX, prototyping, visual design, mobile apps, and responsive web.
  • A portfolio showing D2C product design leadership, systems thinking, data-driven decision-making, high-quality execution, and measurable product impact.
  • Experience designing products where trust, comprehension, eligibility, pricing, access, personal data, or complex decision-making play a central role.
  • Experience with growth, onboarding, conversion, activation, retention, cross-sell, monetization, or lifecycle journeys, informed by research, data and experimentation.
  • A strong AI-native workflow and informed opinions on how AI can improve design quality, team capacity, and business value.

We’d especially love to see

  • Experience in healthcare, women’s health, telehealth, digital health, insurance, fintech, marketplaces, consumer subscriptions, or another regulated or trust-sensitive domain.
  • Experience designing products involving insurance, benefits, prescriptions, clinical eligibility, payments, care navigation, or personal health information.
  • Experience designing in a competitive direct-to-consumer category where acquisition, conversion, trust, differentiation, and retention all matter.

This is a remote role open to candidates based in the United States, with a strong preference for those based in San Francisco.

The base salary range for this role is $195,000-$230,000 per year. You will also be entitled to equity and benefits. Individual pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, and skillset.

Our teams primarily operate from the New York Metropolitan area, NY, and remotely via San Francisco/Bay Area, CA, Seattle, WA, Boston, MA, Chicago, IL, and Washington, D.C. For those in our New York City office, we encourage in-person collaboration by requiring team members to work onsite three days a week  (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday). For those based in San Francisco/Bay Area, CA, Seattle, WA, Boston, MA, Chicago, IL, and Washington, D.C., we encourage in-person collaboration by requiring team members to attend quarterly Work Together Days within these cities. This policy aims to balance remote work flexibility with the benefits of face-to-face interaction.

If you do not have experience in all of the areas detailed above, we hope that you will share your unique background with us in your application and how it can be additive to our teams.

We remain focused on providing a competitive benefits package for our employees. On top of standards such as employer-covered health, dental, and insurance plan options, we offer an inclusive approach to benefits:

  • Maven for Mavens: access to the full platform and specialists, including care for mental health, reproductive health, family planning and pediatrics.
  • Whole-self care through wellness partnerships

About the Role: 

Care Delivery is the infrastructure that powers how Maven members access care and how our providers deliver it. Every program we run across maternity, fertility, menopause, and pediatrics, depends on it. It's where clinical workflows, provider tooling, and the systems that make care measurable, billable, and scalable at Maven's scale all come together.

We're looking for a Product Manager to help build that platform: the EHR and clinical tooling, provider workflows, messaging, and the data and billing infrastructure that turn Maven's care model into something reliable and scalable. You'll own defined capabilities within the platform and drive them from problem to shipped, in close partnership with engineering, clinical, design, and operations. It's a high-leverage seat. What you build here touches every program Maven offers.

You'll report to the Group Product Manager, Care Delivery, and work closely with our providers, as well as Clinical Product, Member Experience, Operations, and the Data and AI Platform teams.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own specific Care Delivery capabilities end-to-end, provider workflows, clinical documentation, messaging, scheduling and matching, or quality and billing infrastructure, from problem definition through launch and iteration.
  • Make crisp, well-reasoned product decisions, especially where clinical accuracy and provider experience are both at stake.
  • Use AI hands-on to move faster, prototyping with AI tools to test ideas and pressure-test flows before committing engineering time, and identify and build AI-powered capabilities into the care delivery platform where they genuinely improve the provider or member experience.
  • Partner daily with engineering and design to ship reliable platform capabilities, and with clinical and operations partners so that what you build works for real providers and members.
  • Translate regulatory and quality requirements, like HEDIS measures and clinical coding, into clean product experiences that add value without adding friction.
  • Instrument what you ship, watch how it performs, and iterate. Bring data to every decision.
  • Build platform primitives, reusable capabilities that serve many programs, rather than one-off features.
  • Bring a point of view on how AI can improve care delivery workflows, and put it to work in how you build.

What You’ll Bring: 

  • 3+ years in product management, ideally with some time in healthcare tech or another complex, regulated, or operations-heavy domain.
  • A strong executor: you take ambiguous problems, break them down, and ship, without needing everything defined for you.
  • Solid data instincts: you define the right metrics, work with real datasets, and communicate findings clearly to both clinical and commercial audiences.
  • Comfort with technical and clinical complexity: you can hold your own in an engineering sprint and a clinical review, and you're eager to learn the domain fast (FHIR, interoperability, EHR workflows).
  • Genuine care for providers and members: the people using what you build show up in your decisions.
  • Clear, direct communication and strong cross-functional collaboration.
  • Fluency with AI and a genuine desire to build with it: you understand how modern AI models work well enough to know where they're reliable and where they aren't, you reach for AI tools to prototype and think, and you're excited to ship AI-powered features rather than just talk about them.
  • Bonus: experience with EHR or EMR systems, clinical workflows, healthcare interoperability, or provider-facing tools.

The base salary range for this role is 155,000-185,000 per year. You will also be entitled to receive equity and benefits. Individual pay decisions are based on qualifications, experience, and skillset.

About The Role:

It's about identifying the right problems, setting and fully owning the design vision for multiple complex areas, making strategic calls under ambiguity, and leading high-impact initiatives that raise the bar for the team around you.

You'll bring deep AI fluency and use it to move faster, explore more broadly, and build more intelligently, while also mentoring others on how to work that way.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the end-to-end experience across complex, cross-functional initiatives for our provider tooling and virtual clinic experience, from early concept through delivery, demonstrating exceptional decision-making and strategic thinking about scope, sequencing, and tradeoffs to drive results across projects.
  • Define how AI should behave in high-stakes contexts: how it communicates uncertainty, when it defers to human care, and how it builds trust with members navigating emotionally charged decisions.
  • Build functional, high-fidelity prototypes using AI-assisted coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code, or similar), and push others to move beyond static mockups.
  • Develop scalable AI-powered patterns in a healthcare context — confidence indicators, human-AI handoffs, progressive disclosure — that become the standard across Maven's design system.
  • Partner with Engineering, Product, Clinical, and Data at a strategic level: shaping model outputs into intuitive interfaces, influencing how problems are framed, and driving alignment across teams.
  • Develop leaders within the design team and non-design partners, fostering independence, delegating effectively, and promoting leadership among peers.
  • Identify and resolve cross-functional tensions, bridging gaps between design, clinical, and product perspectives.
  • Strengthen community within and outside the design team by championing company-wide cultural initiatives.

What You'll Bring:

  • AI fluency: You use AI tools daily (Claude, Figma AI, Cursor, or similar) with strong prompting and synthesis skills. You're also helping others develop that muscle.
  • Vibe coding: You can turn ideas into working prototypes using AI-assisted coding tools, and you're comfortable pushing the boundaries of what that looks like in a healthcare context.
  • Technical depth: You've shipped code to production and can have an informed conversation about backend architecture, model behavior, and system constraints.
  • Strategic craft: A portfolio that shows not just design quality but also evidence of strategic ownership: defining success metrics, navigating ambiguity, and influencing direction.
  • Cross-functional leadership: You've driven complex projects across multiple teams and know how to create momentum without direct authority.
  • Mobile and web: Experience designing for mobile applications and responsive web.
  • Systems thinking: Ability to think beyond a flow and communicate a holistic system that can scale for any program
  • Appetite for complexity: Energized by ambiguity and solving complex problems, and comfortable making calls when the path isn't clear.

Mindset:

  • Deeply empathetic toward members and the providers who help them navigate their family building experience, a space that's emotionally intense, medically complex, and often uncertain.
  • AI-native: you think in terms of what AI makes newly possible, and you bring others along in that thinking.
  • Invested in the people around you. You want the team to be better because you're on it, and to make the team better by mentoring.

Nice To Have:

  • Background working with ML and AI teams on model-driven products.

jobs.title: Director of Product - Secure File Gateway and ICAP
jobs.description_html:
OPSWAT, a global leader in IT, OT, and ICS critical infrastructure cybersecurity, delivers an end-to-end platform that gives public and private sector organizations and enterprises the critical advantage needed to protect their complex networks, secure their devices, and ensure compliance. Over the last 20 years our commitment to innovative technology has earned the trust of more than 1,700 organizations, governments, and institutions globally, solidifying our role in protecting the world’s critical infrastructure and securing our way of life.

Why This Role Matters

At OPSWAT, protecting the world’s critical infrastructure is not an abstract mission. It is real, urgent, and growing. Our ICAP product is a proven, high-impact solution that is trusted by customers who depend on us to secure their most critical systems.  We are now ready to take ICAP to the next level. 

This Director role is a rare opportunity to shape the future of ICAP, including the evolution toward a next-generation Proxy, while scaling commercial impact and deepening customer value. You will operate at the intersection of product strategy, engineering execution, and go-to-market success, with clear ownership and visible impact.  If you are energized by building success, driving innovation, and owning outcomes, this role was designed for you.  

What You Will Be Doing

As Director of AI Product Management, you will be the end-to-end owner of ICAP’s product strategy and growth trajectory.  

You will: 

  • Set and own the ICAP product vision and roadmap, including the strategic evolution into a Proxy-focused solution. 
  • Translate market signals, customer needs, and competitive insights into clear product direction and prioritized investments. 
  • Partner deeply with Engineering, ensuring fast, high-quality execution and scalable architecture. 
  • Work closely with Sales, Sales Engineering, and Marketing to drive bookings, pipeline, and customer adoption. 
  • Serve as a strong, visible product leader across regions, with a close partnership with our Vietnam-based teams. 
  • Balance innovation with operational excellence, ensuring ICAP continues to deliver reliability, performance, and trust at scale. 
  • Represent ICAP with confidence to customers, partners, and internal leadership. 

What Success Looks Like

In your first 12–18 months, success will look like: 

  • A clear, compelling ICAP roadmap aligned to market demand and customer value. 
  • Measurable growth in bookings and pipeline tied directly to product strategy. 
  • Strong, trust-based partnerships with Engineering and GTM teams. 
  • Progress toward a Proxy-focused architecture that positions ICAP for long-term growth. 
  • A product organization that moves with urgency, clarity, and accountability. 

Who You Are

You are a product leader who blends strategic thinking with hands-on execution. 

You bring: 

  • Proven experience leading enterprise or security products at scale. 
  • Deep hands on experience building with AI. 
  • Strong understanding of proxy technologies, ICAP, networking, or adjacent security domains. 
  • A track record of partnering effectively with Engineering to deliver complex products. 
  • Commercial acumen and experience supporting bookings, pipeline, and customer conversations. 
  • Comfort operating in a global, distributed environment, including close collaboration with teams in Vietnam. 
  • Clear, confident communication and the ability to influence across functions. 
  • A mindset rooted in ownership, urgency, and continuous improvement. 
  • Director-level experience is preferred, but we value demonstrated leadership altitude, judgment, and impact above title alone.

Why OPSWAT?

OPSWAT is a fast-growing cybersecurity company with a strong culture of ownership and innovation. We build products that matter, support leaders who take initiative, and invest in those who want to grow. 

In this role, you will:

jobs.description_html:
OPSWAT, a global leader in IT, OT, and ICS critical infrastructure cybersecurity, delivers an end-to-end platform that gives public and private sector organizations and enterprises the critical advantage needed to protect their complex networks, secure their devices, and ensure compliance. The Position

We're assembling a small founding team to build something genuinely hard: high-throughput services that inspect live traffic, terminate and analyze TLS in the data path, and hold near-zero latency while doing it. This is real systems engineering — streaming, distributed, latency-obsessed — not another CRUD app behind a form. 

You won't be starting cold. You inherit real infrastructure and real users, which means what you build reaches production in weeks, not years. The work is high-leverage from day one, and there's nowhere to hide — in the best way. 

AI-native. Non-negotiable.  You leverage AI to operate as a 10x engineer — demonstrable AI proficiency is a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have. 

What You'll Own

You take a capability from a rough idea all the way to production, and then you keep it alive and healthy there — meeting its latency and reliability targets, instrumented well enough to prove it, and hardened to survive real load and real failure. You own the outcome, not the ticket. You'll lead a functional area end to end: set its technical direction, make the calls that matter, and pull other engineers along with you. 

Who You Are 

  • You see what needs to exist and you go build it — you spot the gap, scope it yourself, and start, instead of waiting for someone to hand you a task or a spec. 
  • You lead by taking the hardest, least-defined part of the problem and making it work, and others follow because your judgment and output earn it — not because of a title. 
  • You own the entire arc — design, build, ship, operate — and you treat what happens in production as your responsibility, making sure the system behaves exactly within the parameters it's supposed to, not just that it passed in staging. 
  • When you hit the edge of what you know — a protocol you've never touched, a failure mode you've never seen — curiosity and sheer grit carry you across it faster than most people expect. 
  • "Good enough" makes you uncomfortable; you hold a high bar for yourself and ship work you're genuinely proud to put your name on. 

What You Bring

  • Proven, demonstrable proficiency using AI as a force multiplier — you already operate as a 10x engineer, orchestrating AI tools and agents to design, build, and ship far beyond what you could alone, while keeping the judgment to know what "correct" actually looks like. 
  • 5–7+ years building and operating production services and front ends, with real experience owning something end to end and carrying the weight of it once it's in front of real users. 
  • Hands-on experience with TLS / MITM inspection and the security-sensitive edge cases that come with sitting in the middle of live traffic. 
  • A real track record of taming latency in streaming and distributed systems — you've chased down p99 tail latency and know that "fast on my machine" means nothing until it's fast in production, under load, with observability to back it up. 
  • Strong command of a modern backend language (Go, Rust, or TypeScript/Node) and React/TypeScript on the front end, with a deep working grasp of HTTP, TLS, gRPC/REST, and async/streaming I/O.

jobs.title: Senior Director of Product Management, MetaDefender Endpoint
jobs.description_html:
OPSWAT, a global leader in IT, OT, and ICS critical infrastructure cybersecurity, delivers an end-to-end platform that gives public and private sector organizations and enterprises the critical advantage needed to protect their complex networks, secure their devices, and ensure compliance. Over the last 20 years our commitment to innovative technology has earned the trust of more than 1,700 organizations, governments, and institutions globally, solidifying our role in protecting the world’s critical infrastructure and securing our way of life.

Reports to: Chief Product Officer (CPO)

Scope: Full ownership of the MetaDefender Endpoint portfolio — commercial and community  | Partners daily with global R&D  |  Global / Remote-friendly 

The Position 

Join a pre-IPO, global cybersecurity leader at the forefront of innovation. We protect the unseen — the infrastructure that powers our way of life. OPSWAT protects the world’s critical infrastructure across IT, OT, and ICS environments, trusted by more than 2,000 organizations, governments, and institutions worldwide. 

We are seeking an exceptional product leader to own the vision, strategy, and execution of MetaDefender Endpoint — the endpoint foundation that delivers peripheral media protection, advanced compliance, remote access control, vulnerability detection, and patch management to secure critical assets and maintain organizational security. This is a senior leadership role with end-to-end ownership of a broad endpoint portfolio spanning multiple high-value use cases, every endpoint agent flavor across desktop and mobile, a free global community edition, and a platform strategy that other OPSWAT product lines build on. You will set the roadmap, work hands-on with top global R&D teams every day, and build the business and partnerships that scale endpoint across the globe. 

The Product & Portfolio 

MetaDefender Endpoint secures devices inside critical IT and OT networks and powers a portfolio of endpoint use cases. This role owns that portfolio end to end: 

  • Peripheral Media Protection: the foundational use case — scanning and sanitizing removable media and peripheral devices before their content can be accessed, protecting devices inside critical IT and OT networks from USB and removable-media threats. 
  • Advanced Compliance: continuous endpoint posture and compliance assessment — verifying device health, configuration, and security controls against regulatory frameworks and organizational policy, with audit-ready evidence. 
  • Vulnerability Assessment: continuous asset inspection and file-based vulnerability assessment with CVSS-based risk prioritization to surface the vulnerabilities that matter most, before and after software is installed. 
  • Patch Management: a strategic growth direction for the company — centralized patch management across on-premises, air-gapped, and cloud environments, automatically patching third-party applications and OS updates on flexible schedules and with audit-ready evidence. 
  • Zero Trust Access: real-time device posture and compliance checks that feed continuous, least-privilege, per-application access — layering device health onto identity so every access decision reflects who the user is and whether their device is healthy. 
  • Endpoint as a platform: the shared endpoint foundation that OPSWAT’s other product lines — such as Managed File Transfer, Network Access Control, and Endpoint Malware Scanning — build their endpoint capabilities on, so each team ships on a single, common endpoint architecture without losing the agility and domain expertise it owns. 

The role owns every flavor of the endpoint agent — from Windows and macOS desktop clients to iOS and Android mobile apps — delivering a consistent endpoint experience across desktop and mobile platforms. 

Beyond the commercial offering, this role also stewards the free MetaDefender Endpoint community — an open, no-cost download that lets anyone experience OPSWAT’s technologies firsthand — growing adoption, gathering feedback, and building a pipeline into the commercial portfolio. 

About This Role 

This is a hands-on, technically-engaged product leadership role — not a pure strategy or coordination seat. You own the full endpoint portfolio across its commercial use cases, every agent flavor, and its community edition, and you are accountable for the outcomes: adoption, growth, and customer success. You partner with global R&D on a day-to-day basis — in the details of architecture, prioritization, and release — and you champion the platform strategy that lets multiple use-case teams build on a shared endpoint foundation while preserving each team’s speed and expertise. You bring an AI-first mindset, leveraging AI in the day-to-day work of the team to maximize efficiency and output. You build, mentor, and lead a team of product manager, product designer, product marketing, and engineering professionals, set the bar for product excellence, and represent endpoint to customers, partners, and executive leadership. 

What You Will Be Doing 

  • Own product vision & strategy: define, refine, and champion the vision and roadmap for the MetaDefender Endpoint portfolio — compliance and patch management, zero trust access, and vulnerability management — aligned to business goals and evolving market conditions. 
  • Drive patch and compliance as a growth engine: make centralized, cross-environment patch management (including air-gapped and OT) a flagship direction, and translate it into differentiated roadmap and go-to-market. 
  • Champion the endpoint platform: lead the strategy to establish MetaDefender Endpoint as the single architecture that use-case teams (e.g., Managed File Transfer, Network Access Control, and Endpoint Malware Scanning) develop on — enabling reuse and consistency while protecting each team’s agility and ownership of its business goals. 
  • Own every agent flavor: drive a consistent, high-quality endpoint experience across all agent platforms — Windows and macOS desktop clients and iOS and Android mobile apps. 
  • Lead with an AI-first mindset: bring AI into the day-to-day work of the product organization — from research and requirements to analysis and delivery — to maximize efficiency and output across the team. 
  • Grow and steward the community edition: own the free MetaDefender Endpoint community experience end to end — adoption, engagement, feedback loops, and conversion into commercial value. 
  • Work hands-on with R&D: partner with global R&D teams daily — writing crisp requirements, making trade-offs, and driving execution through to high-quality, timely releases. 
  • Build business and partnerships: develop the business case, pricing, and packaging, and cultivate technology and channel partnerships that expand endpoint’s reach and ecosystem. 
  • Lead market & competitive analysis: stay ahead of emerging trends, assess competitive products, and identify customer needs to inform prioritization and positioning. 
  • Drive user-centered development: advocate for the end user by gathering feedback, analyzing usage data, and driving continuous improvement in usability, functionality, and satisfaction. 
  • Orchestrate cross-functional delivery: partner closely with engineering, sales, marketing, and support to deliver high-quality releases and seamless integration into the broader OPSWAT portfolio. 
  • Track performance: establish clear KPIs, monitor product and adoption performance, and use insights to guide enhancements across both commercial and community. 
  • Communicate with stakeholders: clearly articulate strategy, updates, and results to internal teams, executive leadership, and customers — fostering alignment and enthusiasm. 
  • Build and lead the team: build, mentor, and lead a high-performing, cross-disciplinary team of product managers, product designers, product marketing, and engineering professionals, setting a strong bar for product craft and execution. 

What We Need From You 

  • Product leadership experience: 10+ years in product management with several years leading and growing PM teams, ideally within cybersecurity, endpoint, or infrastructure software. 
  • Broad endpoint portfolio ownership: a track record managing a wide range of endpoint use cases — such as compliance, patch management, vulnerability management, and secure/zero-trust access — not a single narrow feature area. 
  • Deep domain knowledge: strong grasp of cybersecurity, endpoint security best practices, data protection, threat prevention, patch and vulnerability management, and device posture/compliance. 
  • Hands-on and technical: comfortable working shoulder-to-shoulder with R&D day to day, engaging credibly on architecture and trade-offs, and going deep in the product rather than staying at the surface. 
  • Multi-platform endpoint experience: experience delivering endpoint or agent software across operating systems and device types — Windows and macOS desktop, and iOS and Android mobile. 
  • Platform product thinking: experience building or evolving a shared platform that multiple teams develop on, balancing consistency and reuse with team autonomy and speed. 
  • AI-first ways of working: an AI-first mindset — you actively apply AI tools to your own and your team’s daily work to move faster and raise quality. 
  • Community / product-led growth: experience growing a free, community, or product-led offering and converting adoption into commercial outcomes is a strong plus. 
  • Business & partnership builder: demonstrated ability to build the business — pricing, packaging, GTM — and to establish technology and channel partnerships. 
  • Track record of delivery: proven experience managing products from concept through launch, with results in user adoption, revenue growth, or market penetration. 
  • Analytical & decisive: strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills with a data-driven approach. 
  • Exceptional communicator: outstanding interpersonal and executive communication skills, enabling collaboration across cross-functional teams and credibility with customers and leadership. 
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Business, or a related field; MBA is a plus. 
  • Ways of working: familiarity with Agile methodologies or similar frameworks. 

Why You’ll Love Working Here 

  • Own a strategic, high-visibility portfolio at a pre-IPO, global cybersecurity leader — endpoint sits at the center of compliance, patch, vulnerability, and zero-trust access. 
  • Shape a platform: the endpoint architecture and practices you establish will enable product lines across OPSWAT. 
  • Run both a commercial business and a global free community that puts OPSWAT technology in the hands of users everywhere. 
  • Work hands-on with world-class global R&D teams on products that protect critical infrastructure. 
  • Global reach, a high-growth mindset, and the chance to shape products that matter. 
  • Attractive compensation with regular performance assessments and flexibility for the right candidate.

The team works directly with Todd McKinnon, Okta's co-founder and CEO, with the opportunity to bring this product to Okta's 20,000+ customers. You will help shape the product with the ownership and pace of a startup and the resources of a public company.

You will build the harnesses and evaluations that make these workers reliable. They investigate risk, use tools, wait for approvals and complete tasks across enterprise systems. Bring depth in agent execution or model quality and help turn it into working software customers can trust.

About You

Production builder: You have shipped AI software and know what changes when real users depend on it.

Careful evaluator: You investigate failures and use evidence to judge quality.

Strong owner: You follow an improvement through code, evaluation, release and customer use.

What you will be doing

  • Build the agent harness for planning, tool use, memory, context compaction, interruption and recovery during long-running work.
  • Integrate OpenAI and Anthropic model APIs. Select models using measured quality, latency and cost, with clear failure handling.
  • Evaluate existing harnesses and build only the missing pieces. Keep the harness connected to AWS workflow execution and approval state.
  • Keep authorization and sensitive writes behind application policy checks. Require evidence of the resulting state before marking work complete.
  • Build evaluation datasets and replay tests for valid findings, access decisions, app setup and AI agent onboarding.
  • Measure false positives, missed risks, unsafe actions, completion rate and cost. Turn production failures into regression tests.
  • Test prompt injection, stale evidence, conflicting instructions and unsafe tool use. Protect tenant boundaries in retrieval and memory.
  • Improve prompts, retrieval, tools and model routing. Evaluate fine-tuning or other post-training methods when results justify them and data use is approved.

What you will bring to the role

  • Strong Python engineering skills and experience shipping an LLM application that uses tools.
  • Hands-on experience building agent workflows or evaluation systems for tool-using LLM applications. For harness work, relevant experience includes Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Codex SDK, Strands Agents, LangChain Deep Agents, LangGraph or a custom implementation.
  • Experience integrating model APIs, structured outputs and asynchronous services. Experience with OpenAI or Anthropic is especially relevant.
  • Depth in agent execution or evaluation systems, with working code and failure analysis you can explain.
  • Ability to distinguish a plausible model response from a supported finding or verified action.

Scope by level

Principal: Set product engineering direction across workflows and implement the shared components that help the team ship faster.

Our stack

Our core stack is Python FastAPI, AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, PostgreSQL on Amazon RDS and pgvector. OpenAI and Anthropic model APIs are part of the integration plan.

We plan to add an agent harness and a dedicated analytics layer using ClickHouse or BigQuery. The harness choice is open. Experience with equivalent tools also counts.

And extra credit for

  • Open-source contributions, agent observability, security evaluations or synthetic evaluation data.
  • Fine-tuning, preference data, post-training evaluation or model distillation using approved datasets.
  • Identity and security workflows. Foundation-model research experience is optional.

As a designer on this team, you'll own key workflows end-to-end, from early-stage concepting of novel interaction models (there's no established pattern library for "agentic permissioning" yet) to hardening flows for scale as the product matures. You'll partner closely with product managers, engineers, researchers, and content designers, and work closely with our Principal and Staff designers, to turn ambiguous, highly technical agentic problems such as delegation, policy, audit, and trust boundaries between humans and agents into experiences that feel simple and safe. You'll be expected to bring sound design judgment to problems that don't have precedent to borrow from, and to actively experiment with how AI can be woven into your own design process, from exploration to prototyping.

What you will do

  • Own key workflows end-to-end, from early-stage concepting of novel interaction models, where few established patterns exist yet, through hardening and polishing flows as the product matures and scales to millions of customers.
  • Bring a systems-thinking lens to connect user insights with business goals, creating experiences that keep customers and their users and AI agents safe every day in this rapidly evolving space.
  • Design experiences across multiple personas i.e Security Admins, AI Engineers, Enterprise End-users, and IT Admins, tackling complex scenarios like AI agent lifecycle management, permission scoping, human-in-the-loop authorization, and policy enforcement across the Okta portfolio.
  • Contribute to scalable, usable design patterns for non-human identity and agent management and security that hold up under scale, meet a high bar for quality, and improve consistency across the product.
  • Regularly present work, concepts, and new ideas to cross-functional partners and senior leadership, driving alignment and gathering input to sharpen your designs.
  • Actively experiment with AI in your design process, using AI tools for brainstorming, rapid prototyping, exploring edge cases, and iterating on solutions, while developing judgment on where AI genuinely accelerates the work versus where it doesn't, and sharing those learnings with the team.

What we are looking for

  • You keep user goals at the heart of your solutions, while skillfully balancing business objectives and engineering constraints.
  • You stay grounded in delivering real user value even when moving fast and are able to connect the dots across a fast-moving, high-stakes portfolio without losing sight of the person on the other end of the workflow.
  • You move fluidly between big-picture systems thinking and detail-oriented execution, equally comfortable mapping how a workflow fits into the broader agentic AI landscape as you are polishing a single interaction.
  • You thrive in ambiguous environments and are energized by defining patterns, user flows, and system paradigms where none exist yet.
  • You treat iteration as the method, not a fallback. This space has few existing parallels to draw from, requirements shift as the underlying technology evolves, and the only reliable way forward is shipping, learning, and adapting quickly rather than waiting for certainty.
